title: History - Rubin
snippet: History - Rubin ## History of Rubin Glass Factory ## Sixty years of traditions in glassmaking, combined with the most modern technology With over 60 years of history in glassmaking, Rubin is one of the most advanced and established glass producers in the Balkan region. We combine our vast experience and traditions with the latest technological advancements in the industry to produce glass packaging of perfect quality. 1965 ##### The Beginning of Glass Production In July 1965, glass packaging production began in the city of Pleven under the name "Gen. Ivan Vinarov." The official inauguration took place on November 10 of the same year. The factory started operations with two main production workshops, each equipped with two glass furnaces and a total of 17 production lines. Three furnaces operated with clear glass, and one with colored (green) glass. 1965 1972 ##### Expansion into the Largest Facility in the Balkans The design and construction of a new workshop began, featuring two larger glass furnaces, each equipped with six production lines. As a result of this development, the factory became the largest producer of packaging glass in the Balkan Peninsula at that time, specializing in bottles and jars. 1972 1975 ##### Transition to Natural Gas for Greater Efficiency The factory transitioned to natural gas via a gasification process, replacing liquid fuels. This resulted in a significant improvement in energy efficiency and production sustainability. 1975 1985 ##### Peak Industrial Growth and Workforce Expansion At its peak, the facility operated five active furnaces and 26 production lines. The workforce exceeded 1,500 employees, establishing the factory as a key industrial center in the Pleven region. 1985 1991 ##### Rebranding as “RUBIN” The factory officially adopted the name “RUBIN,” which remains its registered trade name to this day. 1991 2007 ##### Full Modernization of Clear Glass Production A large-scale investment was made to fully renovate and modernize of the production equipment in the clear glass facility. This step introduced new technologies, resulting in productivity and enhanced product quality. 2007 2012 ##### Upgrade of the Colored Glass Unit A new investment was made to fully upgrade the colored glass production unit. The main equipment was replaced, and innovative solutions to optimize production processes were introduced. 2012 2015 ##### Streamlined Production with Two Furnaces As of this year, the factory operates two production furnaces — one for clear glass and one for colored — serviced by seven production lines. The total annual production capacity exceeds 190 million glass containers. 2015 2018–2020 ##### Technological Leap and Infrastructure Growth New infrastructure and technological upgrades were realized, as part of a major investment project. This included the delivery and installation of a raw materials conveyor system, the construction of recycling systems (closed-loop cycle), the expansion of production buildings, and the commissioning of two high-efficiency furnaces — No. 5 and No. 6 — for clear and colored glass. In July 2018, Furnace No. 6 was launched — a new-generation installation for colored glass, developed by the German company SORG. In March 2020, Furnace No. 5 was also put into operation for the production of clear packaging glass. The combined capacity of both furnaces reaches 450 tons of molten glass per 24 hours. 2018–2020 2023 ##### Largest Expansion in Company History A new large-scale project has been initiated to expand production capacity with the construction of an additional high-performance Furnace No. 3, with a capacity exceeding 300 tons of glass per day.
